concept_html:
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) answers a question from your own documents in three steps. Retrieve the passages most related to the question. Put them in the prompt. Ask the model to answer from those passages alone, citing each one it uses. The answer then rests on your methodology notes, not on the model's training data. This module covers chunking here, retrieval in B21-L2 and the grounded prompt in B21-L3.

Retrieval works on chunks, not whole documents. A 40-page methodology report covers dozens of topics, so one vector for the whole report matches everything a little and nothing well.

  • Split on structure first. Headings and paragraphs mark where topics change. Split there, then cut any long section by size.
  • Choose a size, then test it. Size counts the tokens of your embedding model. In these exercises, words stand in for tokens. Small chunks match precisely but lose context, such as the table a sentence refers to. Large chunks keep context but blur the match and use more of the prompt. Compare two or three sizes on a retrieval evaluation set (lesson B22-L1) and keep the best.
  • Overlap the windows. With size 200 and overlap 50, each window starts 150 words after the last, so text near a boundary appears in two chunks with context on both sides.
  • Keep the tail, once. The last window is often shorter than size. Keep it, but do not add a window that holds only words the previous one already has.
  • Keep metadata. Store each chunk with its document ID, section heading and position. Citations, filters and re-indexing all need them. A stable ID such as methodology_v4#weighting#2 lets you re-index only the documents that changed.

A sliding window over words:

words = text.split()
step = size - overlap
starts = range(0, max(len(words) - overlap, 1), step)
chunks = [" ".join(words[i:i + size]) for i in starts]

A start at len(words) - overlap or later adds nothing new.

lines: from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Chunk:
"""One retrievable passage. Grain: one window of one section."""
chunk_id: str
doc_id: str
section: str
text: str
def chunk_words(text: str, size: int, overlap: int) -> list[str]:
"""Split text into overlapping windows of words.
Args:
text: The section text.
size: Words per window.
overlap: Words shared by neighbouring windows.
Returns:
Windows in order. The last may be shorter than size.
Raises:
ValueError: If size is not positive or overlap is not in [0, size).
"""
if size <= 0 or not 0 <= overlap < size:
raise ValueError(f"need size > 0 and 0 <= overlap < size, got {size}, {overlap}")
words = text.split()
if not words:
return []
step = size - overlap
return [" ".join(words[i:i + size]) for i in range(0, max(len(words) - overlap, 1), step)]
def chunk_section(doc_id: str, section: str, text: str, size: int, overlap: int) -> list[Chunk]:
"""Chunks of one section, with stable IDs for citations and re-indexing."""
return [
Chunk(chunk_id=f"{doc_id}#{section}#{n}", doc_id=doc_id, section=section, text=window)
for n, window in enumerate(chunk_words(text, size, overlap))
]

exercises.solution:
def chunk_words(text: str, size: int, overlap: int) -> list[str]:
    """Split text into overlapping windows of words.

    Args:
        text: The section text.
        size: Words per window.
        overlap: Words shared by neighbouring windows.

    Returns:
        Windows in order. The last may be shorter than size.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If size is not positive or overlap is not in [0, size).
    """
    if size <= 0 or not 0 <= overlap < size:
        raise ValueError(f"need size > 0 and 0 <= overlap < size, got {size}, {overlap}")
    words = text.split()
    if not words:
        return []
    step = size - overlap
    return [" ".join(words[i:i + size]) for i in range(0, max(len(words) - overlap, 1), step)]

title: Chunk documents for retrieval
why_html: A team's first assistant over its methodology library stored each report as one vector. Asked for the minimum base for regional cuts, it found the right report, the sampling guide. But only the first pages fitted in the prompt, and the rule sat on page 31, so the model said the guide did not cover it. With chunks per section, the one paragraph that held the rule would have been retrieved and quoted.
